title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in Cypress, Harris County sheriff's deputies mistook two 19-year-olds, Anthony and Julian, for car thieves. Deputies surrounded their Camaro, drew guns, and handcuffed them. At least five patrol cars and a helicopter were involved, according to doorbell footage. Deputies had been looking for a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies. Flock cameras had picked up the stolen car's plates, but an undercover deputy and helicopter could not read the plates on the car they stopped, so backup was called. After handcuffing the men, deputies realized it was the wrong car. Julian said a deputy pushed him down and threatened to shoot and kill him, and he showed cuts and scrapes.

Anthony's mother, Leslie, wants deputies held accountable and plans to hire an attorney. The Harris County Sheriff's Office said supervisors, including the district captain, shift lieutenants, and shift sergeants, will review body-worn camera video to check that procedures and protocols were followed. A spokesperson said the men were given information on filing a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
